title: Dementia Risk Reduction in Midlife: A Life-Course, Multidomain Approach Across Dementia Subtypes
content: Dementia risk reduction is a life-course public health opportunity, and midlife offers a particularly valuable time to act. Everyday, achievable steps support brain health and general health together: keeping blood pressure, cholesterol and blood glucose in a healthy range, staying physically active, maintaining a healthy weight, avoiding smoking, limiting alcohol, looking after hearing, mood and social connection, and reducing exposure to air pollution. This narrative review presents a practical, multidomain approach for adults aged 40–65 years across the main forms of dementia, grounded in the 2024 Lancet Commission, the 2026 World Health Organization (WHO) guidelines and randomised trials of multidomain, blood pressure and hearing interventions. Five infographics translate the evidence into accessible tools covering dementia forms and prevention, alignment with the WHO 2026 guidelines, early signs and when to seek help, facts and support services for Australia, and awareness and support for people living with dementia and their carers. Together they show that coordinated action across several areas can help prevent or delay dementia and improve healthy ageing.
